title: 燃料价格翻倍：美国航司盈利承压，低成本模式还能撑多久？
speaker: George Ferguson

segments.en: Yeah, I think the other carriers are going to operate in their financial best interest, right? And so I think they'll want to pick up customers.
segments.zh: 其他航司会从自身财务利益出发，希望吸纳客户。

segments.en: They'd like to pick up a loyal customer. That's not typically what you get out of these low-cost carriers like Frontier and Spirit, right? This is not those well-heeled folks that are filling the loyalty program at Delta.
segments.zh: 他们想要忠诚客户，但边疆和精神航空的客户并非达美那种高价值常旅客。

segments.en: So they may provide small incentives to try to bring them over. But my guess is they're going to act largely in their financial interest.
segments.zh: 他们可能会提供小优惠吸引客户，但主要还是从自身财务利益出发。

segments.en: It's a very challenging market right now, right? Ferris have moved, sorry, fuel has moved, toy, it's doubled. And the airlines have to recoup that in order to stay profitable. None of them will be as profitable in two queue, if you believe they're guidance, as they were in the last two queue.
segments.zh: 当前市场极具挑战，燃料价格翻倍，航司需弥补成本才能盈利，二季度盈利恐不及上季度。

segments.en: So they're really scraping to try to find ways to boost ferris, boost revenues. And I think they'll use the opportunity to increase ferris. Looking at this sector, looking at these ultra-low-cost carriers, there was this meeting in Washington, I think about a week and a half ago with the Transportation Secretary, so you had the CEOs of a leagant and Frontier in some country going to Washington to make their case. What does that say to you about the health of this sector broadly?
segments.zh: 他们正努力寻找提升票价和收入的方法，可能会利用这个机会提价。超低成本航司CEO们曾赴华盛顿与交通部长会面，这反映出该行业面临的压力。
